brief.summary: T-001 is ready to integrate. I re-read the workspace: greeting.js has 3 lines, greet is a named export on lines 1-3, and the only other files are README.md and .git. There is no package.json and no tests. No service check results were provided, so no tests were run and none are claimed as passed. The acceptance criterion (names the files read) and the user's line-count request are both met, no files were changed, and there are no open findings. I did not open README.md myself. I propose a follow-up task, T-002, to add shout(s) after greet in greeting.js, with tests. The owner must decide three things first. (1) Output contract: recommend shout(s) returns s.toUpperCase() with no extra punctuation. (2) Non-string input: recommend leaving it undefined, so a TypeError on null or undefined is acceptable. (3) Test setup: recommend a minimal package.json with type module and the built-in node --test runner, because without it Node treats greeting.js as CommonJS and the export syntax fails to import. T-002 is in scope for the shout export, package.json and one test file. It is out of scope for any change to greet, new dependencies and other greeting functions. Its acceptance criteria are shout('hello') returns 'HELLO'; mixed case is uppercased; shout('') returns ''; spaces and punctuation are preserved; greet('Ada') still returns 'Hello, Ada'; and a test-run check result shows the tests passing.

Proposed follow-up T-003: document greet() in README.md only. It should show the signature greet(name), name as a string, the return value 'Hello, <name>' with no ending punctuation, and the example import { greet } from './greeting.js'; greet('Ada') -> 'Hello, Ada'. Out of scope: any change to greeting.js, validation, and tests. Acceptance: the README shows all of the above, the example output matches the source exactly, greeting.js is unchanged, and optionally the example is run with node and the real output reported. Owner decision needed: whether to document that omitting name returns 'Hello, undefined'. Options are A, document it as current behaviour; B, omit it; C, fix greet() first in a separate code task.
